title: Aggregate activation drop does not identify a rollback effect
prompt: Investigate the activation drop in {activation-mix.csv}. These are synthetic counts for two complete seven-day periods, using the same definition: eligible accounts that activated within seven days. Follow-up is complete. Each account belongs to exactly one segment; the segments cover everyone. A product release happened between periods. Quantify what changed and tell me whether these data justify rolling it back. Use the file and show your calculation.

required.text: States overall activation changed from 68% to 37%, a decline of 31 percentage points.
States returning improved from 80% to 85% and new improved from 20% to 25%.
States returning share changed from 80% to 20% and new share from 20% to 80%.
Reports the symmetric decomposition: mix contribution minus 36 percentage points and within-segment contribution plus 5 percentage points, reconciling to minus 31 points.
Says the release's causal effect and the effect of rolling it back are both unknown from these data, and does not recommend rollback without identifying evidence.

forbidden.text: Claims or implies that the release helped, harmed, caused the mix shift, caused the aggregate decline, or had no effect, without identifying causal evidence.
Claims or implies that rolling back would or would not reverse the mix shift, improve activation, worsen activation, or remove only a beneficial change, without identifying causal evidence.
